statement: (i) Prove that $\sin A+\sin B=2\sin\frac{A+B}{2}\cos\frac{A-B}{2}$. (ii) Hence express $\sin 5\theta+\sin 3\theta$ as a product. (iii) Solve $\sin 5\theta+\sin 3\theta=\sin\theta$ for $0\le\theta\le\pi$.
solution: (i) Add $\sin A=\sin(\frac{A+B}{2}+\frac{A-B}{2})$ and $\sin B=\sin(\frac{A+B}{2}-\frac{A-B}{2})$; the cosine terms double and the sine terms cancel, giving $2\sin\frac{A+B}{2}\cos\frac{A-B}{2}$. (ii) With $A=5\theta,B=3\theta$: $2\sin 4\theta\cos\theta$. (iii) $2\sin4\theta\cos\theta=\sin\theta$. Write $\sin4\theta=2\sin2\theta\cos2\theta=4\sin\theta\cos\theta\cos2\theta$, so $8\sin\theta\cos^{2}\theta\cos2\theta=\sin\theta$. Thus $\sin\theta=0$ or $8\cos^{2}\theta\cos2\theta=1$. $\sin\theta=0\Rightarrow\theta=0,\pi$. The second gives $8c^{2}(2c^{2}-1)=1$ with $c=\cos\theta\Rightarrow 16c^{4}-8c^{2}-1=0\Rightarrow c^{2}=\frac{1+\sqrt{2}}{4}$ (positive root). So $\cos\theta=\pm\sqrt{\frac{1+\sqrt{2}}{4}}$, giving two more solutions in $[0,\pi]$. Total five solutions.
